argument_summary: The current record does not support clean, unqualified certification, but it does support a narrower certification position: the release can be defended on aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents only if the audit packet expressly discloses the unresolved mortgage-servicing hardship-forbearance limitation and states that the runbook is still draft and incomplete. That reframing answers the overbroad part of the concern without claiming the draft mitigation already satisfies policy.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation is not necessary if the auditor is willing to treat this as caveated compliance rather than a failed certification record. The remaining uncertainty is bounded and can be managed through disclosed limitation language and follow-through on the mitigation package, instead of converting the matter into a broader launch-stop dispute on the present record.
claims_about_policy: The policy text does not permit treating a draft runbook, dashboard, or future monitoring plan as equivalent to an approved mitigation. It does permit a compliant record that distinguishes launch-readiness evidence from disclosure obligations. On the admissible evidence, aggregate readiness and no severity-one incidents support readiness, while the unresolved named use-case slice and inconsistent model-card draft trigger a disclosure requirement unless there is approved risk acceptance or a completed approved mitigation package. The proper policy reading is therefore caveated certification with accurate disclosure, not clean certification.
concessions: The present record does not support any statement that there are no known material limitations.
The present record does not support any claim that the draft runbook already removes the disclosure requirement.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or a completed approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
